Stores a value into the atomic integer if the current value is the same as
the `current` value.

The return value is a result indicating whether the new value was written and
containing the previous value. On success this value is guaranteed to be equal to
`current`.

`compare_exchange` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory
ordering of this operation.

`success` describes the required ordering for the
read-modify-write operation that takes place if the comparison with `current` succeeds.
`failure` describes the required ordering for the load operation that takes place when
the comparison fails. Using [as success ordering makes the store part of this operation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The failure ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-2)Panics

Panics if `failure` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicI16, Ordering};
let some_var = AtomicI16::new(5);
assert_eq!(
    some_var.compare_exchange(5, 10, Ordering::Acquire, Ordering::Relaxed),
    Ok(5),
);
assert_eq!(some_var.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 10);
assert_eq!(
    some_var.compare_exchange(6, 12, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::Acquire),
    Err(10),
);
assert_eq!(some_var.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 10);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4787)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4787)

Stores a value into the atomic integer if the current value is the same as
the `current` value.
Unlike [ compare_exchange](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI16.html#method.compare_exchange)
this function is allowed to spuriously fail even
when the comparison succeeds, which can result in more efficient code on some
platforms. The return value is a result indicating whether the new value was
written and containing the previous value.

`compare_exchange_weak` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory
ordering of this operation.

`success` describes the required ordering for the
read-modify-write operation that takes place if the comparison with `current` succeeds.
`failure` describes the required ordering for the load operation that takes place when
the comparison fails. Using [as success ordering makes the store part of this operation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The failure ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-3)Panics

Panics if `failure` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-9)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicI16, Ordering};
let val = AtomicI16::new(4);
let mut old = val.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
loop {
    let new = old * 2;
    match val.compare_exchange_weak(old, new, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::Relaxed) {
        Ok(_) => break,
        Err(x) => old = x,
    }
}
```

`and` takes an [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) argument which describes the memory ordering
of this operation. All ordering modes are possible. Note that using

`Release`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`This function may generate more efficient code than `fetch_and` on some platforms.

- x86/x86_64: `lock and`instead of`cmpxchg`loop ({8,16,32}-bit atomics on x86, but additionally 64-bit atomics on x86_64)
- MSP430: `and`instead of disabling interrupts ({8,16}-bit atomics)

Note: On x86/x86_64, the use of either function should not usually affect the generated code, because LLVM can properly optimize the case where the result is unused.

[makes the store part of this operation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the load part](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`This function may generate more efficient code than `fetch_or` on some platforms.

- x86/x86_64: `lock or`instead of`cmpxchg`loop ({8,16,32}-bit atomics on x86, but additionally 64-bit atomics on x86_64)
- MSP430: `or`instead of disabling interrupts ({8,16}-bit atomics)

Note: On x86/x86_64, the use of either function should not usually affect the generated code, because LLVM can properly optimize the case where the result is unused.

assert_eq!(foo.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 0b111111);

Fetches the value, and applies a function to it that returns an optional
new value. Returns a `Result` of `Ok(previous_value)` if the function returned `Some(_)`, else
`Err(previous_value)`.

Note: This may call the function multiple times if the value has been changed from other threads in
the meantime, as long as the function returns `Some(_)`, but the function will have been applied
only once to the stored value.

`fetch_update` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory ordering of this operation.
The first describes the required ordering for when the operation finally succeeds while the second
describes the required ordering for loads. These correspond to the success and failure orderings of

[respectively.](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI16.html#method.compare_exchange)

`compare_exchange`Using [ Acquire](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire) as success ordering makes the store part
of this operation

`Relaxed`[makes the final successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The (failed) load ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#considerations)Considerations

This method is not magic; it is not provided by the hardware.
It is implemented in terms of [ compare_exchange_weak](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI16.html#method.compare_exchange_weak),
and suffers from the same drawbacks.
In particular, this method will not circumvent the

[ABA Problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABA_problem).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-21)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicI16, Ordering};
let x = AtomicI16::new(7);
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |_| None), Err(7));
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |x| Some(x + 1)), Ok(7));
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |x| Some(x + 1)), Ok(8));
assert_eq!(x.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 9);
```

Returns a mutable pointer to the underlying integer.

Returning an `*mut` pointer from a shared reference to this atomic is
safe because the atomic types work with interior mutability. Any use of
the returned raw pointer requires an `unsafe` block and has to uphold
the safety requirements. If there is concurrent access, note the following
additional safety requirements:

- If this atomic type is [lock-free](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI16.html#method.is_lock_free), any concurrent operations on it must be atomic.
- Otherwise, any concurrent operations on it must be compatible with operations performed by this atomic type.

This is `const fn` on Rust 1.58+.

# AtomicI32 in portable_atomic - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/portable-atomic/^1/struct.AtomicI32.html

`pub struct AtomicI32 { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An integer type which can be safely shared between threads.

This type has the same in-memory representation as the underlying integer type,
[ i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html).

If the compiler and the platform support atomic loads and stores of [ i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html), this type is a wrapper for the standard library’s

`AtomicI32`. If the platform supports it but the compiler does not, atomic operations are implemented using
inline assembly. Otherwise synchronizes using global locks.
You can call [to check whether atomic instructions or locks will be used.](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI32.html#method.is_lock_free)

`AtomicI32::is_lock_free()`## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Creates a new reference to an atomic integer from a pointer.

This is `const fn` on Rust 1.83+.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

- `ptr`must be aligned to- `align_of::<AtomicI32>()`(note that on some platforms this can be bigger than- `align_of::<i32>()`).
- `ptr`must be- [valid](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ptr/index.html#safety)for both reads and writes for the whole lifetime- `'a`.
- If this atomic type is [lock-free](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI32.html#method.is_lock_free), non-atomic accesses to the value behind`ptr`must have a happens-before relationship with atomic accesses via the returned value (or vice-versa).- In other words, time periods where the value is accessed atomically may not overlap with periods where the value is accessed non-atomically.
- This requirement is trivially satisfied if `ptr`is never used non-atomically for the duration of lifetime`'a`. Most use cases should be able to follow this guideline.
- This requirement is also trivially satisfied if all accesses (atomic or not) are done from the same thread.

- If this atomic type is *not*lock-free:- Any accesses to the value behind `ptr`must have a happens-before relationship with accesses via the returned value (or vice-versa).
- Any concurrent accesses to the value behind `ptr`for the duration of lifetime`'a`must be compatible with operations performed by this atomic type.

- Any accesses to the value behind
- This method must not be used to create overlapping or mixed-size atomic accesses, as these are not supported by the memory model.

#### pub const fn [is_always_lock_free](https://docs.rs#method.is_always_lock_free)() -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Returns `true` if operations on values of this type are lock-free.

If the compiler or the platform doesn’t support the necessary atomic instructions, global locks for every potentially concurrent atomic operation will be used.

**Note:** If the atomic operation relies on dynamic CPU feature detection,
this type may be lock-free even if the function returns false.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::AtomicI32;
const IS_ALWAYS_LOCK_FREE: bool = AtomicI32::is_always_lock_free();
```
Returns a mutable reference to the underlying integer.

This is safe because the mutable reference guarantees that no other threads are concurrently accessing the atomic data.

This is `const fn` on Rust 1.83+.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicI32, Ordering};
let mut some_var = AtomicI32::new(10);
assert_eq!(*some_var.get_mut(), 10);
*some_var.get_mut() = 5;
assert_eq!(some_var.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 5);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4792)

#### pub const fn [into_inner](https://docs.rs#method.into_inner)(self) -> [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)

Consumes the atomic and returns the contained value.

This is safe because passing `self` by value guarantees that no other threads are
concurrently accessing the atomic data.

This is `const fn` on Rust 1.56+.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::AtomicI32;
let some_var = AtomicI32::new(5);
assert_eq!(some_var.into_inner(), 5);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4792)

Stores a value into the atomic integer if the current value is the same as
the `current` value.

The return value is a result indicating whether the new value was written and
containing the previous value. On success this value is guaranteed to be equal to
`current`.

`compare_exchange` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory
ordering of this operation.

`success` describes the required ordering for the
read-modify-write operation that takes place if the comparison with `current` succeeds.
`failure` describes the required ordering for the load operation that takes place when
the comparison fails. Using [as success ordering makes the store part of this operation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The failure ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-2)Panics

Panics if `failure` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicI32, Ordering};
let some_var = AtomicI32::new(5);
assert_eq!(
    some_var.compare_exchange(5, 10, Ordering::Acquire, Ordering::Relaxed),
    Ok(5),
);
assert_eq!(some_var.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 10);
assert_eq!(
    some_var.compare_exchange(6, 12, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::Acquire),
    Err(10),
);
assert_eq!(some_var.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 10);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4792)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4792)

Stores a value into the atomic integer if the current value is the same as
the `current` value.
Unlike [ compare_exchange](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI32.html#method.compare_exchange)
this function is allowed to spuriously fail even
when the comparison succeeds, which can result in more efficient code on some
platforms. The return value is a result indicating whether the new value was
written and containing the previous value.

`compare_exchange_weak` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory
ordering of this operation.

`success` describes the required ordering for the
read-modify-write operation that takes place if the comparison with `current` succeeds.
`failure` describes the required ordering for the load operation that takes place when
the comparison fails. Using [as success ordering makes the store part of this operation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The failure ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-3)Panics

Panics if `failure` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-9)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicI32, Ordering};
let val = AtomicI32::new(4);
let mut old = val.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
loop {
    let new = old * 2;
    match val.compare_exchange_weak(old, new, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::Relaxed) {
        Ok(_) => break,
        Err(x) => old = x,
    }
}
```

assert_eq!(foo.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 0b011110);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4792)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4792)

Fetches the value, and applies a function to it that returns an optional
new value. Returns a `Result` of `Ok(previous_value)` if the function returned `Some(_)`, else
`Err(previous_value)`.

Note: This may call the function multiple times if the value has been changed from other threads in
the meantime, as long as the function returns `Some(_)`, but the function will have been applied
only once to the stored value.

`fetch_update` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory ordering of this operation.
The first describes the required ordering for when the operation finally succeeds while the second
describes the required ordering for loads. These correspond to the success and failure orderings of

[respectively.](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI32.html#method.compare_exchange)

`compare_exchange`Using [ Acquire](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire) as success ordering makes the store part
of this operation

[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the final successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The (failed) load ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-4)Panics

Panics if `fetch_order` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#considerations)Considerations

This method is not magic; it is not provided by the hardware.
It is implemented in terms of [ compare_exchange_weak](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI32.html#method.compare_exchange_weak),
and suffers from the same drawbacks.
In particular, this method will not circumvent the

[ABA Problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABA_problem).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-21)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicI32, Ordering};
let x = AtomicI32::new(7);
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |_| None), Err(7));
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |x| Some(x + 1)), Ok(7));
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |x| Some(x + 1)), Ok(8));
assert_eq!(x.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 9);
```

Returns a mutable pointer to the underlying integer.

Returning an `*mut` pointer from a shared reference to this atomic is
safe because the atomic types work with interior mutability. Any use of
the returned raw pointer requires an `unsafe` block and has to uphold
the safety requirements. If there is concurrent access, note the following
additional safety requirements:

- If this atomic type is [lock-free](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI32.html#method.is_lock_free), any concurrent operations on it must be atomic.
- Otherwise, any concurrent operations on it must be compatible with operations performed by this atomic type.

This is `const fn` on Rust 1.58+.

# AtomicI64 in portable_atomic - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/portable-atomic/^1/struct.AtomicI64.html

`pub struct AtomicI64 { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An integer type which can be safely shared between threads.

This type has the same in-memory representation as the underlying integer type,
[ i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html).

If the compiler and the platform support atomic loads and stores of [ i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html), this type is a wrapper for the standard library’s

`AtomicI64`. If the platform supports it but the compiler does not, atomic operations are implemented using
inline assembly. Otherwise synchronizes using global locks.
You can call [to check whether atomic instructions or locks will be used.](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI64.html#method.is_lock_free)

`AtomicI64::is_lock_free()`## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Creates a new reference to an atomic integer from a pointer.

This is `const fn` on Rust 1.83+.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

- `ptr`must be aligned to- `align_of::<AtomicI64>()`(note that on some platforms this can be bigger than- `align_of::<i64>()`).
- `ptr`must be- [valid](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ptr/index.html#safety)for both reads and writes for the whole lifetime- `'a`.
- If this atomic type is [lock-free](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI64.html#method.is_lock_free), non-atomic accesses to the value behind`ptr`must have a happens-before relationship with atomic accesses via the returned value (or vice-versa).- In other words, time periods where the value is accessed atomically may not overlap with periods where the value is accessed non-atomically.
- This requirement is trivially satisfied if `ptr`is never used non-atomically for the duration of lifetime`'a`. Most use cases should be able to follow this guideline.
- This requirement is also trivially satisfied if all accesses (atomic or not) are done from the same thread.

- If this atomic type is *not*lock-free:- Any accesses to the value behind `ptr`must have a happens-before relationship with accesses via the returned value (or vice-versa).
- Any concurrent accesses to the value behind `ptr`for the duration of lifetime`'a`must be compatible with operations performed by this atomic type.

- Any accesses to the value behind
- This method must not be used to create overlapping or mixed-size atomic accesses, as these are not supported by the memory model.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4797)

Stores a value into the atomic integer if the current value is the same as
the `current` value.

The return value is a result indicating whether the new value was written and
containing the previous value. On success this value is guaranteed to be equal to
`current`.

`compare_exchange` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory
ordering of this operation.

`success` describes the required ordering for the
read-modify-write operation that takes place if the comparison with `current` succeeds.
`failure` describes the required ordering for the load operation that takes place when
the comparison fails. Using [as success ordering makes the store part of this operation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The failure ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-2)Panics

Panics if `failure` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicI64, Ordering};
let some_var = AtomicI64::new(5);
assert_eq!(
    some_var.compare_exchange(5, 10, Ordering::Acquire, Ordering::Relaxed),
    Ok(5),
);
assert_eq!(some_var.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 10);
assert_eq!(
    some_var.compare_exchange(6, 12, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::Acquire),
    Err(10),
);
assert_eq!(some_var.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 10);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4797)

Stores a value into the atomic integer if the current value is the same as
the `current` value.
Unlike [ compare_exchange](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI64.html#method.compare_exchange)
this function is allowed to spuriously fail even
when the comparison succeeds, which can result in more efficient code on some
platforms. The return value is a result indicating whether the new value was
written and containing the previous value.

`compare_exchange_weak` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory
ordering of this operation.

`success` describes the required ordering for the
read-modify-write operation that takes place if the comparison with `current` succeeds.
`failure` describes the required ordering for the load operation that takes place when
the comparison fails. Using [as success ordering makes the store part of this operation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The failure ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-3)Panics

Panics if `failure` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-9)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicI64, Ordering};
let val = AtomicI64::new(4);
let mut old = val.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
loop {
    let new = old * 2;
    match val.compare_exchange_weak(old, new, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::Relaxed) {
        Ok(_) => break,
        Err(x) => old = x,
    }
}

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4797)

Fetches the value, and applies a function to it that returns an optional
new value. Returns a `Result` of `Ok(previous_value)` if the function returned `Some(_)`, else
`Err(previous_value)`.

Note: This may call the function multiple times if the value has been changed from other threads in
the meantime, as long as the function returns `Some(_)`, but the function will have been applied
only once to the stored value.

`fetch_update` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory ordering of this operation.
The first describes the required ordering for when the operation finally succeeds while the second
describes the required ordering for loads. These correspond to the success and failure orderings of

[respectively.](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI64.html#method.compare_exchange)

`compare_exchange`Using [ Acquire](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire) as success ordering makes the store part
of this operation

[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the final successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The (failed) load ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-4)Panics

Panics if `fetch_order` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#considerations)Considerations

This method is not magic; it is not provided by the hardware.
It is implemented in terms of [ compare_exchange_weak](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI64.html#method.compare_exchange_weak),
and suffers from the same drawbacks.
In particular, this method will not circumvent the

[ABA Problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABA_problem).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-21)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicI64, Ordering};
let x = AtomicI64::new(7);
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |_| None), Err(7));
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |x| Some(x + 1)), Ok(7));
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |x| Some(x + 1)), Ok(8));
assert_eq!(x.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 9);
```

```
If you want to obtain the maximum value in one step, you can use the following:

```

Returns a mutable pointer to the underlying integer.

Returning an `*mut` pointer from a shared reference to this atomic is
safe because the atomic types work with interior mutability. Any use of
the returned raw pointer requires an `unsafe` block and has to uphold
the safety requirements. If there is concurrent access, note the following
additional safety requirements:

- If this atomic type is [lock-free](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI64.html#method.is_lock_free), any concurrent operations on it must be atomic.
- Otherwise, any concurrent operations on it must be compatible with operations performed by this atomic type.

This is `const fn` on Rust 1.58+.

# AtomicI128 in portable_atomic - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/portable-atomic/^1/struct.AtomicI128.html

`pub struct AtomicI128 { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An integer type which can be safely shared between threads.

This type has the same in-memory representation as the underlying integer type,
[ i128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i128.html).

If the compiler and the platform support atomic loads and stores of [ i128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i128.html), this type is a wrapper for the standard library’s

`AtomicI128`. If the platform supports it but the compiler does not, atomic operations are implemented using
inline assembly. Otherwise synchronizes using global locks.
You can call [to check whether atomic instructions or locks will be used.](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI128.html#method.is_lock_free)

`AtomicI128::is_lock_free()`## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4802)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-AtomicI128)### impl [AtomicI128](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI128.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4802)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-AtomicI128)

### impl [AtomicI128](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI128.html)

Creates a new reference to an atomic integer from a pointer.

This is `const fn` on Rust 1.83+.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

- `ptr`must be aligned to- `align_of::<AtomicI128>()`(note that on some platforms this can be bigger than- `align_of::<i128>()`).
- `ptr`must be- [valid](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ptr/index.html#safety)for both reads and writes for the whole lifetime- `'a`.
- If this atomic type is [lock-free](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI128.html#method.is_lock_free), non-atomic accesses to the value behind`ptr`must have a happens-before relationship with atomic accesses via the returned value (or vice-versa).- In other words, time periods where the value is accessed atomically may not overlap with periods where the value is accessed non-atomically.
- This requirement is trivially satisfied if `ptr`is never used non-atomically for the duration of lifetime`'a`. Most use cases should be able to follow this guideline.
- This requirement is also trivially satisfied if all accesses (atomic or not) are done from the same thread.

- If this atomic type is *not*lock-free:- Any accesses to the value behind `ptr`must have a happens-before relationship with accesses via the returned value (or vice-versa).
- Any concurrent accesses to the value behind `ptr`for the duration of lifetime`'a`must be compatible with operations performed by this atomic type.

- Any accesses to the value behind
- This method must not be used to create overlapping or mixed-size atomic accesses, as these are not supported by the memory model.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4802)

Stores a value into the atomic integer if the current value is the same as
the `current` value.

The return value is a result indicating whether the new value was written and
containing the previous value. On success this value is guaranteed to be equal to
`current`.

`compare_exchange` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory
ordering of this operation.

`success` describes the required ordering for the
read-modify-write operation that takes place if the comparison with `current` succeeds.
`failure` describes the required ordering for the load operation that takes place when
the comparison fails. Using [as success ordering makes the store part of this operation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The failure ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-2)Panics

Panics if `failure` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicI128, Ordering};
let some_var = AtomicI128::new(5);
assert_eq!(
    some_var.compare_exchange(5, 10, Ordering::Acquire, Ordering::Relaxed),
    Ok(5),
);
assert_eq!(some_var.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 10);
assert_eq!(
    some_var.compare_exchange(6, 12, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::Acquire),
    Err(10),
);
assert_eq!(some_var.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 10);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4802)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4802)

Stores a value into the atomic integer if the current value is the same as
the `current` value.
Unlike [ compare_exchange](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI128.html#method.compare_exchange)
this function is allowed to spuriously fail even
when the comparison succeeds, which can result in more efficient code on some
platforms. The return value is a result indicating whether the new value was
written and containing the previous value.

`compare_exchange_weak` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory
ordering of this operation.

`success` describes the required ordering for the
read-modify-write operation that takes place if the comparison with `current` succeeds.
`failure` describes the required ordering for the load operation that takes place when
the comparison fails. Using [as success ordering makes the store part of this operation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The failure ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-3)Panics

Panics if `failure` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-9)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicI128, Ordering};
let val = AtomicI128::new(4);
let mut old = val.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
loop {
    let new = old * 2;
    match val.compare_exchange_weak(old, new, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::Relaxed) {
        Ok(_) => break,
        Err(x) => old = x,
    }
}
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4802)

Fetches the value, and applies a function to it that returns an optional
new value. Returns a `Result` of `Ok(previous_value)` if the function returned `Some(_)`, else
`Err(previous_value)`.

Note: This may call the function multiple times if the value has been changed from other threads in
the meantime, as long as the function returns `Some(_)`, but the function will have been applied
only once to the stored value.

`fetch_update` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory ordering of this operation.
The first describes the required ordering for when the operation finally succeeds while the second
describes the required ordering for loads. These correspond to the success and failure orderings of

[respectively.](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI128.html#method.compare_exchange)

`compare_exchange`Using [ Acquire](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire) as success ordering makes the store part
of this operation

[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the final successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The (failed) load ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-4)Panics

Panics if `fetch_order` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#considerations)Considerations

This method is not magic; it is not provided by the hardware.
It is implemented in terms of [ compare_exchange_weak](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI128.html#method.compare_exchange_weak),
and suffers from the same drawbacks.
In particular, this method will not circumvent the

[ABA Problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABA_problem).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-21)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicI128, Ordering};
let x = AtomicI128::new(7);
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |_| None), Err(7));
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |x| Some(x + 1)), Ok(7));
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |x| Some(x + 1)), Ok(8));
assert_eq!(x.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 9);
```

Returns a mutable pointer to the underlying integer.

Returning an `*mut` pointer from a shared reference to this atomic is
safe because the atomic types work with interior mutability. Any use of
the returned raw pointer requires an `unsafe` block and has to uphold
the safety requirements. If there is concurrent access, note the following
additional safety requirements:

- If this atomic type is [lock-free](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicI128.html#method.is_lock_free), any concurrent operations on it must be atomic.
- Otherwise, any concurrent operations on it must be compatible with operations performed by this atomic type.

This is `const fn` on Rust 1.58+.

# AtomicIsize in portable_atomic - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/portable-atomic/^1/struct.AtomicIsize.html

`pub struct AtomicIsize { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An integer type which can be safely shared between threads.

This type has the same in-memory representation as the underlying integer type,
[ isize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.isize.html).

If the compiler and the platform support atomic loads and stores of [ isize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.isize.html), this type is a wrapper for the standard library’s

`AtomicIsize`. If the platform supports it but the compiler does not, atomic operations are implemented using
inline assembly. Otherwise synchronizes using global locks.
You can call [to check whether atomic instructions or locks will be used.](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicIsize.html#method.is_lock_free)

`AtomicIsize::is_lock_free()`## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

### impl [AtomicIsize](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicIsize.html)

Creates a new reference to an atomic integer from a pointer.

This is `const fn` on Rust 1.83+.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

- `ptr`must be aligned to- `align_of::<AtomicIsize>()`(note that on some platforms this can be bigger than- `align_of::<isize>()`).
- `ptr`must be- [valid](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ptr/index.html#safety)for both reads and writes for the whole lifetime- `'a`.
- If this atomic type is [lock-free](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicIsize.html#method.is_lock_free), non-atomic accesses to the value behind`ptr`must have a happens-before relationship with atomic accesses via the returned value (or vice-versa).- In other words, time periods where the value is accessed atomically may not overlap with periods where the value is accessed non-atomically.
- This requirement is trivially satisfied if `ptr`is never used non-atomically for the duration of lifetime`'a`. Most use cases should be able to follow this guideline.
- This requirement is also trivially satisfied if all accesses (atomic or not) are done from the same thread.

- If this atomic type is *not*lock-free:- Any accesses to the value behind `ptr`must have a happens-before relationship with accesses via the returned value (or vice-versa).
- Any concurrent accesses to the value behind `ptr`for the duration of lifetime`'a`must be compatible with operations performed by this atomic type.

- Any accesses to the value behind
- This method must not be used to create overlapping or mixed-size atomic accesses, as these are not supported by the memory model.

Stores a value into the atomic integer if the current value is the same as
the `current` value.

The return value is a result indicating whether the new value was written and
containing the previous value. On success this value is guaranteed to be equal to
`current`.

`compare_exchange` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory
ordering of this operation.

`success` describes the required ordering for the
read-modify-write operation that takes place if the comparison with `current` succeeds.
`failure` describes the required ordering for the load operation that takes place when
the comparison fails. Using [as success ordering makes the store part of this operation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The failure ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-2)Panics

Panics if `failure` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicIsize, Ordering};
let some_var = AtomicIsize::new(5);
assert_eq!(
    some_var.compare_exchange(5, 10, Ordering::Acquire, Ordering::Relaxed),
    Ok(5),
);
assert_eq!(some_var.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 10);
assert_eq!(
    some_var.compare_exchange(6, 12, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::Acquire),
    Err(10),
);
assert_eq!(some_var.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 10);
```

Stores a value into the atomic integer if the current value is the same as
the `current` value.
Unlike [ compare_exchange](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicIsize.html#method.compare_exchange)
this function is allowed to spuriously fail even
when the comparison succeeds, which can result in more efficient code on some
platforms. The return value is a result indicating whether the new value was
written and containing the previous value.

`compare_exchange_weak` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory
ordering of this operation.

`success` describes the required ordering for the
read-modify-write operation that takes place if the comparison with `current` succeeds.
`failure` describes the required ordering for the load operation that takes place when
the comparison fails. Using [as success ordering makes the store part of this operation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The failure ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-3)Panics

Panics if `failure` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-9)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicIsize, Ordering};
let val = AtomicIsize::new(4);
let mut old = val.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
loop {
    let new = old * 2;
    match val.compare_exchange_weak(old, new, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::Relaxed) {
        Ok(_) => break,
        Err(x) => old = x,
    }
}
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4773)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4773)

Fetches the value, and applies a function to it that returns an optional
new value. Returns a `Result` of `Ok(previous_value)` if the function returned `Some(_)`, else
`Err(previous_value)`.

Note: This may call the function multiple times if the value has been changed from other threads in
the meantime, as long as the function returns `Some(_)`, but the function will have been applied
only once to the stored value.

`fetch_update` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory ordering of this operation.
The first describes the required ordering for when the operation finally succeeds while the second
describes the required ordering for loads. These correspond to the success and failure orderings of

[respectively.](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicIsize.html#method.compare_exchange)

`compare_exchange`Using [ Acquire](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire) as success ordering makes the store part
of this operation

[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the final successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The (failed) load ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-4)Panics

Panics if `fetch_order` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#considerations)Considerations

This method is not magic; it is not provided by the hardware.
It is implemented in terms of [ compare_exchange_weak](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicIsize.html#method.compare_exchange_weak),
and suffers from the same drawbacks.
In particular, this method will not circumvent the

[ABA Problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABA_problem).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-21)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicIsize, Ordering};
let x = AtomicIsize::new(7);
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |_| None), Err(7));
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |x| Some(x + 1)), Ok(7));
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |x| Some(x + 1)), Ok(8));
assert_eq!(x.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 9);
```

Returns a mutable pointer to the underlying integer.

Returning an `*mut` pointer from a shared reference to this atomic is
safe because the atomic types work with interior mutability. Any use of
the returned raw pointer requires an `unsafe` block and has to uphold
the safety requirements. If there is concurrent access, note the following
additional safety requirements:

- If this atomic type is [lock-free](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicIsize.html#method.is_lock_free), any concurrent operations on it must be atomic.
- Otherwise, any concurrent operations on it must be compatible with operations performed by this atomic type.

This is `const fn` on Rust 1.58+.

# AtomicPtr in portable_atomic - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/portable-atomic/^1/struct.AtomicPtr.html

`pub struct AtomicPtr<T> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A raw pointer type which can be safely shared between threads.

This type has the same in-memory representation as a `*mut T`.

If the compiler and the platform support atomic loads and stores of pointers,
this type is a wrapper for the standard library’s
[ AtomicPtr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/type.AtomicPtr.html). If the platform supports it
but the compiler does not, atomic operations are implemented using inline
assembly.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Creates a new `AtomicPtr` from a pointer.

This is `const fn` on Rust 1.83+.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

- `ptr`must be aligned to- `align_of::<AtomicPtr<T>>()`(note that on some platforms this can be bigger than- `align_of::<*mut T>()`).
- `ptr`must be- [valid](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ptr/index.html#safety)for both reads and writes for the whole lifetime- `'a`.
- If this atomic type is [lock-free](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicPtr.html#method.is_lock_free), non-atomic accesses to the value behind`ptr`must have a happens-before relationship with atomic accesses via the returned value (or vice-versa).- In other words, time periods where the value is accessed atomically may not overlap with periods where the value is accessed non-atomically.
- This requirement is trivially satisfied if `ptr`is never used non-atomically for the duration of lifetime`'a`. Most use cases should be able to follow this guideline.
- This requirement is also trivially satisfied if all accesses (atomic or not) are done from the same thread.

- If this atomic type is *not*lock-free:- Any accesses to the value behind `ptr`must have a happens-before relationship with accesses via the returned value (or vice-versa).
- Any concurrent accesses to the value behind `ptr`for the duration of lifetime`'a`must be compatible with operations performed by this atomic type.

- Any accesses to the value behind
- This method must not be used to create overlapping or mixed-size atomic accesses, as these are not supported by the memory model.

Stores a value into the pointer if the current value is the same as the `current` value.

The return value is a result indicating whether the new value was written and containing
the previous value. On success this value is guaranteed to be equal to `current`.

`compare_exchange` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory
ordering of this operation.

`success` describes the required ordering for the
read-modify-write operation that takes place if the comparison with `current` succeeds.
`failure` describes the required ordering for the load operation that takes place when
the comparison fails. Using [as success ordering makes the store part of this operation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The failure ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

Stores a value into the pointer if the current value is the same as the `current` value.

Unlike [ AtomicPtr::compare_exchange](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicPtr.html#method.compare_exchange), this function is allowed to spuriously fail even when the
comparison succeeds, which can result in more efficient code on some platforms. The
return value is a result indicating whether the new value was written and containing the
previous value.

`compare_exchange_weak` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory
ordering of this operation.

`success` describes the required ordering for the
read-modify-write operation that takes place if the comparison with `current` succeeds.
`failure` describes the required ordering for the load operation that takes place when
the comparison fails. Using [as success ordering makes the store part of this operation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The failure ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-3)Panics

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-9)Examples

use portable_atomic::{AtomicPtr, Ordering};
let some_ptr = AtomicPtr::new(&mut 5);

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#2168-2185)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#2168-2185)

Fetches the value, and applies a function to it that returns an optional
new value. Returns a `Result` of `Ok(previous_value)` if the function
returned `Some(_)`, else `Err(previous_value)`.

Note: This may call the function multiple times if the value has been
changed from other threads in the meantime, as long as the function
returns `Some(_)`, but the function will have been applied only once to
the stored value.

`fetch_update` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory
ordering of this operation. The first describes the required ordering for
when the operation finally succeeds while the second describes the
required ordering for loads. These correspond to the success and failure
orderings of

[respectively.](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicPtr.html#method.compare_exchange)

`compare_exchange`Using [ Acquire](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire) as success ordering makes the store part of this
operation

[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the final successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The (failed) load ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-4)Panics

Panics if `fetch_order` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#considerations)Considerations

This method is not magic; it is not provided by the hardware.
It is implemented in terms of [ compare_exchange_weak](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicPtr.html#method.compare_exchange_weak),
and suffers from the same drawbacks.
In particular, this method will not circumvent the

[ABA Problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABA_problem).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-10)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicPtr, Ordering};
let ptr: *mut _ = &mut 5;
let some_ptr = AtomicPtr::new(ptr);
let new: *mut _ = &mut 10;
assert_eq!(some_ptr.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |_| None), Err(ptr));
let result = some_ptr.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |x| {
    if x == ptr {
        Some(new)
    } else {
        None
    }
});
assert_eq!(result, Ok(ptr));
assert_eq!(some_ptr.load(Ordering::SeqCst), new);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#2221-2223)#### pub fn [fetch_ptr_add](https://docs.rs#method.fetch_ptr_add)(&self, val: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html), order: [Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html)) -> [*mut T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#2221-2223)

#### pub fn [fetch_ptr_add](https://docs.rs#method.fetch_ptr_add)(&self, val: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html), order: [Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html)) -> [*mut T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)

Offsets the pointer’s address by adding `val` (in units of `T`),
returning the previous pointer.

This is equivalent to using [ wrapping_add](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.pointer.html#method.wrapping_add) to atomically perform the
equivalent of

`ptr = ptr.wrapping_add(val);`.This method operates in units of `T`, which means that it cannot be used
to offset the pointer by an amount which is not a multiple of
`size_of::<T>()`. This can sometimes be inconvenient, as you may want to
work with a deliberately misaligned pointer. In such cases, you may use
the [ fetch_byte_add](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicPtr.html#method.fetch_byte_add) method instead.

`fetch_ptr_add` takes an [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) argument which describes the
memory ordering of this operation. All ordering modes are possible. Note
that using

`Release`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

Offsets the pointer’s address by subtracting `val` (in units of `T`),
returning the previous pointer.

This is equivalent to using [ wrapping_sub](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.pointer.html#method.wrapping_sub) to atomically perform the
equivalent of

`ptr = ptr.wrapping_sub(val);`.This method operates in units of `T`, which means that it cannot be used
to offset the pointer by an amount which is not a multiple of
`size_of::<T>()`. This can sometimes be inconvenient, as you may want to
work with a deliberately misaligned pointer. In such cases, you may use
the [ fetch_byte_sub](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicPtr.html#method.fetch_byte_sub) method instead.

`fetch_ptr_sub` takes an [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) argument which describes the memory
ordering of this operation. All ordering modes are possible. Note that
using

[makes the store part of this operation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the load part](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-12)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicPtr, Ordering};
let array = [1i32, 2i32];

Returns a mutable pointer to the underlying pointer.

Returning an `*mut` pointer from a shared reference to this atomic is
safe because the atomic types work with interior mutability. Any use of
the returned raw pointer requires an `unsafe` block and has to uphold
the safety requirements. If there is concurrent access, note the following
additional safety requirements:

- If this atomic type is [lock-free](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicPtr.html#method.is_lock_free), any concurrent operations on it must be atomic.
- Otherwise, any concurrent operations on it must be compatible with operations performed by this atomic type.

This is `const fn` on Rust 1.58+.

# AtomicU8 in portable_atomic - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/portable-atomic/^1/struct.AtomicU8.html

`pub struct AtomicU8 { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An integer type which can be safely shared between threads.

This type has the same in-memory representation as the underlying integer type,
[ u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html).

If the compiler and the platform support atomic loads and stores of [ u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html), this type is a wrapper for the standard library’s

`AtomicU8`. If the platform supports it but the compiler does not, atomic operations are implemented using
inline assembly. Otherwise synchronizes using global locks.
You can call [to check whether atomic instructions or locks will be used.](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicU8.html#method.is_lock_free)

`AtomicU8::is_lock_free()`## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Creates a new reference to an atomic integer from a pointer.

This is `const fn` on Rust 1.83+.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

- `ptr`must be aligned to- `align_of::<AtomicU8>()`(note that on some platforms this can be bigger than- `align_of::<u8>()`).
- `ptr`must be- [valid](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ptr/index.html#safety)for both reads and writes for the whole lifetime- `'a`.
- If this atomic type is [lock-free](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicU8.html#method.is_lock_free), non-atomic accesses to the value behind`ptr`must have a happens-before relationship with atomic accesses via the returned value (or vice-versa).- In other words, time periods where the value is accessed atomically may not overlap with periods where the value is accessed non-atomically.
- This requirement is trivially satisfied if `ptr`is never used non-atomically for the duration of lifetime`'a`. Most use cases should be able to follow this guideline.
- This requirement is also trivially satisfied if all accesses (atomic or not) are done from the same thread.

- If this atomic type is *not*lock-free:- Any accesses to the value behind `ptr`must have a happens-before relationship with accesses via the returned value (or vice-versa).
- Any concurrent accesses to the value behind `ptr`for the duration of lifetime`'a`must be compatible with operations performed by this atomic type.

- Any accesses to the value behind
- This method must not be used to create overlapping or mixed-size atomic accesses, as these are not supported by the memory model.

Returns a mutable reference to the underlying integer.

This is safe because the mutable reference guarantees that no other threads are concurrently accessing the atomic data.

This is `const fn` on Rust 1.83+.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicU8, Ordering};
let mut some_var = AtomicU8::new(10);
assert_eq!(*some_var.get_mut(), 10);
*some_var.get_mut() = 5;
assert_eq!(some_var.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 5);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4784)

#### pub const fn [into_inner](https://docs.rs#method.into_inner)(self) -> [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)

Consumes the atomic and returns the contained value.

This is safe because passing `self` by value guarantees that no other threads are
concurrently accessing the atomic data.

This is `const fn` on Rust 1.56+.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::AtomicU8;
let some_var = AtomicU8::new(5);
assert_eq!(some_var.into_inner(), 5);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4784)

Stores a value into the atomic integer if the current value is the same as
the `current` value.

The return value is a result indicating whether the new value was written and
containing the previous value. On success this value is guaranteed to be equal to
`current`.

`compare_exchange` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory
ordering of this operation.

`success` describes the required ordering for the
read-modify-write operation that takes place if the comparison with `current` succeeds.
`failure` describes the required ordering for the load operation that takes place when
the comparison fails. Using [as success ordering makes the store part of this operation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The failure ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-2)Panics

Panics if `failure` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicU8, Ordering};
let some_var = AtomicU8::new(5);
assert_eq!(
    some_var.compare_exchange(5, 10, Ordering::Acquire, Ordering::Relaxed),
    Ok(5),
);
assert_eq!(some_var.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 10);
assert_eq!(
    some_var.compare_exchange(6, 12, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::Acquire),
    Err(10),
);
assert_eq!(some_var.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 10);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4784)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4784)

Stores a value into the atomic integer if the current value is the same as
the `current` value.
Unlike [ compare_exchange](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicU8.html#method.compare_exchange)
this function is allowed to spuriously fail even
when the comparison succeeds, which can result in more efficient code on some
platforms. The return value is a result indicating whether the new value was
written and containing the previous value.

`compare_exchange_weak` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory
ordering of this operation.

`success` describes the required ordering for the
read-modify-write operation that takes place if the comparison with `current` succeeds.
`failure` describes the required ordering for the load operation that takes place when
the comparison fails. Using [as success ordering makes the store part of this operation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The failure ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-3)Panics

Panics if `failure` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-9)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicU8, Ordering};
let val = AtomicU8::new(4);
let mut old = val.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
loop {
    let new = old * 2;
    match val.compare_exchange_weak(old, new, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::Relaxed) {
        Ok(_) => break,
        Err(x) => old = x,
    }
}
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/portable_atomic/lib.rs.html#4784)

Fetches the value, and applies a function to it that returns an optional
new value. Returns a `Result` of `Ok(previous_value)` if the function returned `Some(_)`, else
`Err(previous_value)`.

Note: This may call the function multiple times if the value has been changed from other threads in
the meantime, as long as the function returns `Some(_)`, but the function will have been applied
only once to the stored value.

`fetch_update` takes two [ Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html) arguments to describe the memory ordering of this operation.
The first describes the required ordering for when the operation finally succeeds while the second
describes the required ordering for loads. These correspond to the success and failure orderings of

[respectively.](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicU8.html#method.compare_exchange)

`compare_exchange`Using [ Acquire](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire) as success ordering makes the store part
of this operation

[, and using](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[makes the final successful load](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release)

`Release`[. The (failed) load ordering can only be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.SeqCst)

`SeqCst`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Acquire)

`Acquire`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Relaxed)

`Relaxed`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-4)Panics

Panics if `fetch_order` is [ Release](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.Release),

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html#variant.AcqRel)

`AcqRel`[§](https://docs.rs#considerations)Considerations

This method is not magic; it is not provided by the hardware.
It is implemented in terms of [ compare_exchange_weak](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicU8.html#method.compare_exchange_weak),
and suffers from the same drawbacks.
In particular, this method will not circumvent the

[ABA Problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABA_problem).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-21)Examples

```
use portable_atomic::{AtomicU8, Ordering};
let x = AtomicU8::new(7);
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |_| None), Err(7));
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |x| Some(x + 1)), Ok(7));
assert_eq!(x.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |x| Some(x + 1)), Ok(8));
assert_eq!(x.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 9);
```

Returns a mutable pointer to the underlying integer.

Returning an `*mut` pointer from a shared reference to this atomic is
safe because the atomic types work with interior mutability. Any use of
the returned raw pointer requires an `unsafe` block and has to uphold
the safety requirements. If there is concurrent access, note the following
additional safety requirements:

- If this atomic type is [lock-free](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomicU8.html#method.is_lock_free), any concurrent operations on it must be atomic.
- Otherwise, any concurrent operations on it must be compatible with operations performed by this atomic type.

This is `const fn` on Rust 1.58+.
